stem.text: The Russian wormwood, Artemisia gmelinii, has a stomatal index of 13.8 for its lower leaf surface and 1.7 for its upper leaf surface.
Explain the advantages to the plant for this difference in stomatal index values.

points.text: allows sufficient, carbon dioxide uptake / gaseous exchange ;
reduces, transpiration / water loss ;
stomata on lower surface less exposed to, high light intensity / wind ; ora
allows more space for photosynthesis ;

markScheme.note: Point n follows the order of the transcribed marking points; table rows or source labels such as 3a and 3b retain their original wording.

explanation.text: A lower surface is usually more sheltered than the upper surface. Locating more pores there can permit carbon dioxide entry while limiting the water-vapour gradient maintained by wind over exposed surfaces.

reasoningChain: Compare the upper and lower stomatal indices.
Link the distribution to carbon dioxide supply and reduced evaporative loss.

stem.text: Figure 10.2 is a graph showing changes over a 24-hour period in the carbon dioxide concentration of the air in a glasshouse containing plants. The glasshouse did not have artificial lighting so the only source of light for the plants was sunlight.
The carbon dioxide concentration in the external atmosphere over the 24-hour period is also shown.

The air in the glasshouse was not completely sealed off from the external atmosphere so any difference in the carbon dioxide concentration between the glasshouse and external atmosphere will gradually decrease unless there are processes to maintain the difference.

stem.alt: Carbon dioxide concentrations in a glasshouse and the external atmosphere over 24 hours.

explanation.text: The trace is a concentration, not a direct measurement of photosynthetic rate. Identify when uptake can maintain a low internal concentration despite exchange with outside air, and when diminishing light restricts uptake.

stem.text: ATP and reduced NADP are products of the light-dependent stage of photosynthesis.
State where, in the chloroplasts, ATP and reduced NADP are produced and describe the roles of ATP and reduced NADP in the light-independent stage of photosynthesis.

points.text: thylakoid (membrane) ;
ATP and reduced NADP used to convert GP to TP ;
ATP used in regeneration of RuBP ;

markScheme.note: Point n follows the order of the transcribed marking points; table rows or source labels such as 3a and 3b retain their original wording.

explanation.text: Reduction of GP to TP requires both an energy input and reducing power. Regeneration of the carbon dioxide acceptor RuBP requires ATP, but does not use reduced NADP for that regeneration step.

reasoningChain: Locate production of ATP and reduced NADP at the thylakoids.
Assign their distinct roles to GP reduction and RuBP regeneration.

blocks.heading: Comprehensive responses
bullets: Most responses calculated the answer correctly.

blocks.heading: Comprehensive responses
bullets: Most responses interpreted the different stomatal index values on upper versus lower leaf surfaces with an understanding of the need for water conservation.

blocks.heading: Limited responses
bullets: Some responses only made vague references to transpiration, photosynthesis or light intensity.
Some responses made no reference to gaseous exchange.

blocks.heading: Comprehensive responses
bullets: Some responses linked the correct limiting factors to specific times using the data.

blocks.heading: Limited responses
bullets: Many responses needed more accurate graph interpretation and clearer linkage to limiting factors. Just stating daytime, night-time or during the day or night was not sufficiently precise.
Some responses incorrectly stated that higher carbon dioxide concentrations suggested higher rates of photosynthesis.
Some responses referred to respiration which was not required.

blocks.heading: Comprehensive responses
bullets: Most responses correctly identified the precise location in the chloroplast and described the roles of ATP and NADP.

blocks.heading: Limited responses
bullets: Some responses needed to describe the roles of ATP and reduced NADP more accurately.
A few responses stated the grana more generally or stated the phase of photosynthesis instead of the physical location.
